name: Inchworm
lede: Inchworm is a bright yellow-green named for the looping caterpillar, a Crayola color that replaced an older crayon rather than joining the box as something new.

sections.title: Replacing Magic Mint
sections.body:
An inchworm is a caterpillar that moves by arching its body into a loop and pulling its back half up to its front, as if measuring the ground in inches [1]. Crayola introduced a crayon of this color in 2003, known as "Inch Worm" from 2003 to 2005 before the spelling settled to one word; it replaced the retired color Magic Mint [2]. Our data does not record who chose the name or whether a contest was involved [2].

The nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[kiwi]], more vivid than this shade; [[light-lime]] sits close by, lighter [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Inchworm covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [4]. A yellow-green this bright and this light is rare in oil paint before modern synthetic pigments, and the name itself did not exist before 2003 [2][4]. That describes our museum-sourced archive, not painting as a whole [4].

notes.cite: ColorHub archive (23,781 paintings), computed match, as photographed

questions.q: What color did Inchworm replace in Crayola's lineup?
True or false: a painting from the 1800s could have been described by its maker as "Inchworm green."

openers: Inchworm didn't join Crayola's box; it replaced Magic Mint in 2003.
